dedupe_keys.name: fragility of buried operating steel pipelines under longitudinal permanent ground deformation

description: This model computes analytical fragility functions for buried steel pipelines in operation when the ground moves permanently along the pipe axis, as happens with earthquake-induced landslides or lateral spreading after liquefaction. It was published as a 2024 preprint by Gersena Banushi of the University of California, Berkeley. The analytical pipe model accounts for asymmetric material behaviour in tension and compression under varying operating loads, is validated, and is embedded in a Monte Carlo framework that gives the probability of exceeding performance limit states conditioned on the intensity of permanent ground deformation. The fragility surfaces show higher probabilities for larger soil displacements, longer displaced lengths and deeper cover, because more soil reaction resists pipe deformation, and a global sensitivity analysis highlights ground deformation and soil-pipe interaction parameters. Coverage: generic steel transmission pipelines. Access: open preprint on Preprints.org; no code release found. Licence and cost: CC BY 4.0, free. Caveats: a preprint not yet peer reviewed at the time of reading, one loading mode (longitudinal), and no field damage validation. It supports hazard exposure and resilience analysis of oil and gas pipeline networks in seismic regions, helping operators prioritise mitigation. It complements the SYNER-G fragility curves and the PHMSA incident data in the catalogue.
